explanations.b: Retouch services use the same formula strength as the original service or potentially a gentler formula if the hair shows signs of sensitivity; increasing strength at each retouch would progressively damage hair.
explanations.c: Applying product from scalp to ends at every retouch would double-process the already-relaxed hair at every appointment, causing cumulative protein damage that leads to breakage.
explanations.d: A strand test should be performed before any chemical service if there is uncertainty about the hair's current condition, previous service history, or compatibility with the planned service; prior processing history does not eliminate the need for assessment.

questions.name: Hair Care Services
questions.objective: III.E.5c — Chemical hair relaxing/restructuring and curl reduction: Keratin
questions.text: Keratin smoothing treatments (Brazilian blowouts) differ from traditional relaxers in that

answers.text: they permanently alter the disulfide bonds in the same way as hydroxide relaxers
they require a thio neutralizer to lock in the straightened result
they are temporary or semi-permanent treatments that coat the hair with a keratin protein formula, reducing frizz and curl without breaking disulfide bonds — typically lasting 2–6 months
they are identical to permanent waves but applied at a lower temperature

explanations.a: Keratin smoothing treatments do not break or permanently alter disulfide bonds; they work by depositing keratin protein on and within the hair cuticle and using heat to seal it in place — a mechanical coating process, not a chemical bond-breaking process.
explanations.b: Keratin treatments do not require a thio neutralizer because no reduction of disulfide bonds occurs during the treatment; the straightening mechanism is the deposition and heat-sealing of a coating formula, not the reduction-oxidation chemistry of thio systems.
explanations.c: Keratin smoothing treatments (various brand names including Brazilian Blowout, Coppola Keratin Complex) are semi-permanent coating treatments: they apply a liquid keratin formula to the hair, which is then sealed in with high heat from a flat iron; some formulas contain crosslinking agents (including formaldehyde-releasing compounds in some brands) that temporarily bond the protein coating to the hair; the result reduces frizz and smooths the curl pattern for 2–6 months; because no disulfide bond modification occurs, the natural curl pattern returns as the coating wears away.
explanations.d: Keratin treatments are fundamentally different from permanent waves; permanent waves chemically alter disulfide bonds to create new curl patterns; keratin treatments coat and temporarily smooth existing structure without altering the hair's internal chemistry.

questions.name: Hair Care Services
questions.objective: III.E.5c — Chemical hair relaxing/restructuring and curl reduction: Keratin
questions.text: The primary occupational safety concern when performing keratin smoothing treatments is

answers.text: the high heat of the flat iron used to seal the treatment
the dark color of many keratin formulas that stains work surfaces
the physical weight of keratin solution bottles causing ergonomic strain
formaldehyde or formaldehyde-releasing compounds in some formulas that release toxic vapors when heated with the flat iron

explanations.a: While flat iron heat is a technical concern for the client's hair, it is not the primary occupational health concern; the formaldehyde vapor issue is a more significant health hazard for the barber who is repeatedly exposed.
explanations.b: Surface staining is a minor practical concern; some keratin formulas do stain surfaces, but this is a housekeeping issue rather than a health hazard.
explanations.c: Ergonomic concerns apply to all barbershop services; the weight of keratin product bottles is not the distinctive primary hazard of this specific service.
explanations.d: Many keratin smoothing treatment formulas — particularly first-generation Brazilian blowout products — contain methylene glycol (formaldehyde in solution) or other compounds that release formaldehyde gas when heated with a flat iron (typically at 375–450°F); formaldehyde is a known respiratory irritant and human carcinogen (IARC Group 1); barbers performing these treatments are exposed to significant formaldehyde vapor concentrations in the breathing zone; OSHA has issued warnings and citations related to formaldehyde exposure in salons performing keratin treatments, and many jurisdictions now require specific ventilation, respiratory protection, and product disclosure for these services.

questions.name: Hair Care Services
questions.objective: III.E.5c — Chemical hair relaxing/restructuring and curl reduction: Keratin
questions.text: After a keratin smoothing treatment, clients are advised to avoid washing their hair for 48–72 hours because

answers.text: the keratin formula continues to penetrate the cortex during this period and water would wash it out before it has reached full depth
water and surfactants would disturb the still-curing protein coating before it has fully cross-linked and bonded to the hair structure
washing too soon would cause the treatment to permanently straighten the hair instead of the intended temporary effect
the scalp requires 48–72 hours to produce enough sebum to protect the hair after the treatment

explanations.a: Keratin smoothing treatments do not penetrate the cortex the way chemical relaxers do; the keratin formula coats the cuticle and some enter the surface of the hair shaft; the timing restriction is about allowing the surface coating to cure, not about ongoing deep penetration.
explanations.b: After the flat iron seals the keratin formula into the hair, the coating undergoes a curing process (cross-linking of the protein coating to itself and to the hair surface, particularly in formaldehyde or glyoxylic acid-containing formulas); during the initial 48–72 hour window, this cross-linking process is still occurring; water (which can swell and soften the coating) and shampoo surfactants (which can strip or disrupt the forming protein film) would interfere with the curing process before the coating has achieved its full structural integrity — reducing the longevity and smoothness of the treatment result.
explanations.c: Washing too soon would actually reduce the effectiveness (longevity) of the treatment — it would not cause permanent over-straightening; the treatment is inherently temporary and washing disrupts the surface coating.
explanations.d: Sebum production is a continuous biological process unrelated to keratin treatment aftercare; the 48–72 hour restriction is based on the chemistry of the coating's curing process, not on sebaceous gland activity.

questions.name: Hair Care Services
questions.objective: III.E.5c — Chemical hair relaxing/restructuring and curl reduction: Keratin
questions.text: A client with previously hydroxide-relaxed hair requests a keratin smoothing treatment. The primary consideration is

answers.text: whether the relaxed hair has sufficient protein structure integrity to tolerate heat processing, since chemically relaxed hair is often compromised and additional flat iron heat may cause breakage
the keratin treatment will reverse the relaxer, returning the hair to its natural curl
hydroxide relaxers prevent keratin coating from adhering to the hair shaft
the client must return to their natural state before any keratin treatment can be performed

explanations.a: The structural integrity of the relaxed hair and its ability to tolerate the high flat iron heat required to seal the keratin treatment is the primary clinical consideration; hydroxide-relaxed hair has undergone significant protein modification (lanthionization), which can leave it with reduced strength and heat resistance; performing a keratin treatment on structurally compromised relaxed hair with high heat flat iron passes carries a significant risk of breakage, snap-off, or severe damage.
explanations.b: A keratin smoothing treatment does not reverse a hydroxide relaxer; the lanthionine bonds created by the hydroxide process are permanent — no surface coating treatment can re-establish the original disulfide bond curl pattern.
explanations.c: Hydroxide relaxers modify the cortex but do not create a physical barrier to keratin coating; the cuticle is still accessible to surface depositing products after hydroxide relaxer processing.
explanations.d: Requiring the client to return to natural state before any keratin treatment is an overly restrictive and clinically unsupported position; keratin treatments can be performed on relaxed hair with appropriate assessment of hair integrity — the key is evaluating whether the hair's current condition can tolerate the process.

questions.name: Hair Care Services
questions.objective: III.E.6a — Chemical waving/texturizing: Alkaline
questions.text: Alkaline permanent waves process at room temperature because

answers.text: heat damages the perm rods and must be avoided
ammonium thioglycolate at alkaline pH generates sufficient chemical activity at room temperature to break disulfide bonds without requiring external heat
alkaline waves are heat-activated and require a dryer to process
the alkaline pH neutralizes body heat from the scalp during processing

explanations.a: Heat does not damage standard perm rods; perm rods are made of heat-resistant plastic or rubber designed to tolerate typical processing temperatures; the reason for room-temperature processing is chemical, not equipment-related.
explanations.b: Alkaline permanent waves use ammonium thioglycolate at a pH of approximately 8.2–9.6; at this alkaline pH, the thioglycolate is in its active free thiol form and has sufficient chemical reactivity to open the cuticle and reduce the disulfide bonds in the cortex at room temperature without requiring external heat acceleration; this self-processing ability makes alkaline waves faster and more powerful than acid waves.
explanations.c: Alkaline waves are self-processing at room temperature — the opposite of requiring a dryer; acid waves (not alkaline) typically benefit from added heat (dryer or hood) because glyceryl monothioglycolate at lower pH requires heat to activate.
explanations.d: Body heat from the scalp can mildly accelerate processing at the root area, but the alkaline pH does not 'neutralize' this heat; the chemical reactivity of ammonium thioglycolate at alkaline pH is the reason for room-temperature processing.

questions.name: Hair Care Services
questions.objective: III.E.6a — Chemical waving/texturizing: Alkaline
questions.text: The rod size used in a permanent wave determines

answers.text: the strength of the perm solution required to process the hair
the color of the curl produced by the permanent wave
the processing time regardless of the perm solution formula
the diameter of the curl or wave produced — smaller rods create tighter curls while larger rods produce looser waves

explanations.a: Rod size does not determine perm solution strength; formula strength is selected based on hair texture, porosity, and the desired wave intensity — not on the rod's physical diameter.
explanations.b: Permanent wave rods do not affect hair color; the curl or wave pattern is a structural result of the chemical and mechanical process.
explanations.c: Processing time is determined by the perm solution formula strength, hair's porosity and texture, and ambient temperature — not by the diameter of the rod used.
explanations.d: The rod diameter is the primary physical determinant of the resulting curl or wave diameter: a small rod wraps the hair in a tight circumference, producing a tight, small curl; a large rod wraps the hair in a wide circumference, producing a loose, wide wave; this relationship is governed by the principle that the hair conforms to the shape of the rod as hydrogen bonds reform during drying and neutralization — the tighter the wrap around the rod, the tighter the resulting curl.

questions.name: Hair Care Services
questions.objective: III.E.6a — Chemical waving/texturizing: Alkaline
questions.text: The test curl in a permanent wave service is performed to

answers.text: determine whether the client is allergic to the perm solution before the full application
measure the exact amount of perm solution needed for the entire head
add additional curl to areas that need more processing

check whether the hair has processed sufficiently by unrolling a test rod and observing whether the curl formed matches the rod diameter — indicating the disulfide bonds have broken and the hair has taken the rod shape

explanations.a: Allergy testing is done by a predisposition patch test applied to the skin before the service, not by a test curl; a test curl is a processing assessment technique, not an allergy test.
explanations.b: Perm solution quantity is estimated based on hair density, length, and the number of rods used; a test curl evaluates processing readiness, not solution quantity.
explanations.c: A test curl reads the current processing state — it determines whether to continue processing or neutralize; it does not add additional curl.
explanations.d: The test curl (or S-test) involves unrolling one or more test rods at intervals during processing and gently pushing the unwound hair toward the scalp to observe whether it forms an S-wave or curl pattern that matches the diameter of the rod; when the hair shows a clear S-wave pattern matching the rod size, it has been adequately processed — enough disulfide bonds have been reduced and the hair has physically taken the rod's curl shape; if the curl is still too loose (smaller S than expected), processing continues; this is performed to prevent over-processing (gummy, weak hair) or under-processing (limp, undefined curl).

questions.name: Hair Care Services
questions.objective: III.E.6a — Chemical waving/texturizing: Alkaline
questions.text: Alkaline permanent waves are most appropriate for

answers.text: fine, fragile, or chemically compromised hair that requires the gentlest possible processing
color-treated hair where the cuticle has already been lifted by previous services
resistant, coarse, or low-porosity natural hair that requires the stronger cuticle-lifting power and bond-breaking activity of a higher-pH formula
hair that is longer than 12 inches to ensure the alkaline formula can travel the full length

explanations.a: Fine, fragile, or chemically compromised hair requires the gentlest available perm chemistry — this is the appropriate use case for acid waves or non-thio gentler formulas; alkaline waves on fragile hair cause overprocessing and breakage.
explanations.b: Color-treated hair has an elevated porosity from the color service; the already-open cuticle would allow the more aggressive alkaline perm solution to penetrate too rapidly, causing overprocessing; color-treated hair is better suited to gentler acid or non-thio perm formulas.
explanations.c: Alkaline permanent waves with their higher pH (8.2–9.6) and ammonium thioglycolate reducing agent are specifically suited for resistant, coarse, low-porosity hair with tightly packed cuticles; the higher alkalinity provides the cuticle-swelling power needed to open resistant cuticles and allow the reducing agent to penetrate to the cortex within a practical processing time; attempting to process resistant hair with a mild acid wave would result in underprocessing.
explanations.d: Hair length does not determine which perm formula type is appropriate; the formula selection is based on hair's porosity, texture, and prior chemical history — not on hair length; alkaline waves can be used on any length of resistant natural hair.

questions.name: Hair Care Services
questions.objective: III.E.6b — Chemical waving/texturizing: Acid
questions.text: Acid permanent waves use which active ingredient?

answers.text: Glyceryl monothioglycolate (GMTG)
Sodium hydroxide
Ammonium bisulfite
Guanidine carbonate

explanations.a: Acid permanent waves use glyceryl monothioglycolate (GMTG) as their active reducing agent; GMTG operates at a lower, more hair-friendly pH (approximately 6.5–8.2) compared to the alkaline ammonium thioglycolate of standard alkaline waves; GMTG typically requires the application of heat (from a hood dryer or processing cap) to activate its reducing action because it does not generate sufficient chemical activity at the lower pH to adequately process at room temperature.
explanations.b: Sodium hydroxide is the active ingredient in lye relaxers — not in permanent waves of any type; it is an alkaline compound used for straightening, not waving.
explanations.c: Ammonium bisulfite is a reducing agent used in some hair straightening and curl-reformation products, but it is not the active ingredient in acid permanent waves; glyceryl monothioglycolate (GMTG) is the specific reducing agent formulated for the lower pH (4.5–7.0) environment of acid wave products, providing gentler processing with less cuticle swelling than alkaline wave chemicals.
explanations.d: Guanidine carbonate is the activator component in no-lye guanidine hydroxide relaxers — not in permanent waves; it is a straightening chemical, not a waving agent.

questions.name: Hair Care Services
questions.objective: III.E.6b — Chemical waving/texturizing: Acid
questions.text: Acid permanent waves typically require added heat during processing because

answers.text: heat activates the glyceryl monothioglycolate by increasing its pH to the alkaline range needed for processing
heat causes the perm rods to expand, tightening the curl pattern
glyceryl monothioglycolate at its lower pH requires thermal activation to achieve adequate reducing action on the hair's disulfide bonds within a practical processing time
heat opens the neutralizer prematurely, preventing the need for a separate neutralizing step

explanations.a: Heat does not raise the pH of glyceryl monothioglycolate to an alkaline range; GMTG operates in the acid range (pH 6.5–8.2) throughout processing; the role of heat is to increase the kinetic energy of the reaction, not to change the formula's pH.
explanations.b: Standard plastic or rubber perm rods do not expand meaningfully under the moderate heat of a processing dryer; the curl pattern is determined by the rod's diameter, not by thermal expansion.
explanations.c: Glyceryl monothioglycolate at pH 6.5–8.2 has lower chemical reactivity than ammonium thioglycolate at higher alkaline pH; at this lower pH, GMTG does not spontaneously process at room temperature within a reasonable timeframe; the addition of moderate heat (from a hood dryer at approximately 100–140°F) provides the kinetic energy needed to accelerate the GMTG molecule's reducing action and achieve adequate disulfide bond reduction in the processing time.
explanations.d: Neutralization is a separate chemical step performed after rinsing the perm solution; heat during processing does not trigger neutralization or eliminate the need for a neutralizer.

questions.name: Hair Care Services
questions.objective: III.E.6b — Chemical waving/texturizing: Acid
questions.text: Acid waves are preferred over alkaline waves for color-treated or fine, sensitive hair because

answers.text: they produce tighter, more defined curls than alkaline waves on all hair types
they cost significantly less than alkaline wave products
they require no neutralizer after processing, saving service time
the lower pH causes less cuticle swelling and protein disruption, reducing the risk of over-processing the already-sensitized hair

explanations.a: Acid waves generally produce softer, more natural-looking waves rather than the tighter curls of alkaline waves on the same hair; the gentler chemistry at lower pH is what makes them suitable for sensitized hair, not superior curl tightness.
explanations.b: Product cost is not a clinical consideration in wave formula selection; formula selection is based on the client's hair type, condition, and desired result.
explanations.c: Acid waves require the same neutralizing step as alkaline waves; the oxidizing neutralizer is essential to re-form disulfide bonds in the waved position regardless of whether the processing solution was alkaline or acid-balanced.
explanations.d: The lower pH of acid waves (6.5–8.2 vs. alkaline waves at 8.2–9.6) causes less swelling of the cuticle scales during processing; less cuticle opening means less opportunity for the reducing agent to penetrate excessively into an already-porous and sensitized cortex; this gentler penetration rate reduces the risk of overprocessing fine or color-treated hair, which has a compromised cuticle that is already more permeable than resistant hair; the resulting wave is softer and the hair retains more of its original integrity.

questions.name: Hair Care Services
questions.objective: III.E.6b — Chemical waving/texturizing: Acid
questions.text: A client whose hair was over-processed during an acid wave service would likely present with

answers.text: hair that is extremely springy and coiled tighter than the rod used
hair that is gummy, weak, and overly elastic when wet — stretching without returning to its original length — indicating cortical protein breakdown
hair that remains straight with no wave formation despite the service
an exothermic reaction visible as steam or heat at the hair surface

explanations.a: Extremely tight, springy coils tighter than the rod suggest overprocessing of highly porous hair, but this pattern is more associated with over-processing in some cases; the most reliable clinical sign of over-processing in any perm service is the loss of structural integrity evidenced by the gummy, over-elastic wet hair described in option b.
explanations.b: When perm solution (whether alkaline or acid) over-processes the hair, the reducing agent continues to break disulfide bonds beyond the optimal point; excessive reduction of disulfide bonds depletes the cortical protein scaffold, producing hair that feels gummy (sticky, mushy) and overly elastic when wet — it stretches dramatically without returning to its original length; this is the definitive clinical sign of cortical protein breakdown from over-processing, and it indicates severely compromised structural integrity that may result in breakage during or after neutralization.
explanations.c: Hair that remains straight with no wave formation indicates under-processing (insufficient disulfide bond reduction) — the opposite of over-processing; under-processed hair has too many intact bonds and the hair did not take the rod shape.
explanations.d: An exothermic heat reaction visible as steam is associated with a different chemical incompatibility (such as metallic dyes reacting with hydrogen peroxide) — it is not a characteristic presentation of perm over-processing.

questions.name: Hair Care Services
questions.objective: III.E.6c — Chemical waving/texturizing: Non-thio
questions.text: Non-thio permanent waves use alternative reducing agents such as

answers.text: sodium hydroxide or guanidine hydroxide
hydrogen peroxide or sodium bromate
cysteamine hydrochloride or ammonium bisulfite
resorcinol or para-phenylenediamine

explanations.c: Non-thio (thioglycolate-free) permanent waves use alternative reducing agents that break disulfide bonds through chemistry different from ammonium thioglycolate; common non-thio reducing agents include cysteamine hydrochloride (a naturally occurring aminothiol compound) and ammonium bisulfite (or sodium bisulfite); these alternatives are typically gentler than traditional thioglycolates, produce less odor, and are often marketed for sensitive or color-treated hair where the characteristic thioglycolate smell or strength is undesirable.
explanations.a: Sodium hydroxide and guanidine hydroxide are alkaline agents used in chemical relaxers — they straighten hair through lanthionization; they are not permanent waving agents and do not produce waves.
explanations.b: Hydrogen peroxide and sodium bromate are oxidizing neutralizers used in the neutralization step of permanent waves — they re-form disulfide bonds after the reducing agent has processed; they are not the reducing agents that break bonds during the waving step.
explanations.d: Resorcinol is a coupling agent used in oxidative hair color chemistry; para-phenylenediamine (PPD) is a primary intermediate in oxidative hair dye; neither is a permanent wave reducing agent.

questions.name: Hair Care Services
questions.objective: III.E.6c — Chemical waving/texturizing: Non-thio
questions.text: Non-thio permanent waves are advantageous over thioglycolate waves primarily because

answers.text: they produce stronger, longer-lasting curl results than traditional thio waves
they contain no neutralizer and set the curl through an air-drying mechanism only
they are gentler on sensitive or color-treated hair, produce significantly less odor, and may be better tolerated by clients or technicians with thioglycolate sensitivity
they can be applied to hair previously treated with hydroxide relaxers without chemical incompatibility

explanations.a: Non-thio waves are generally gentler than traditional alkaline thioglycolate waves — they typically produce softer, more natural-looking waves rather than stronger or longer-lasting results; claiming superiority in curl strength and longevity is not accurate.
explanations.b: Non-thio waves do require a neutralizer to re-form the disulfide bonds in the waved position; air drying alone does not achieve the oxidative neutralization needed to lock in the curl pattern.
explanations.c: Non-thio waves offer several client and practitioner advantages: the alternative reducing agents are generally gentler on already-sensitized or color-treated hair where thioglycolate's strength might cause overprocessing; the absence of ammonium thioglycolate eliminates the characteristic strong sulfur-like odor associated with traditional perm services, improving client comfort and the salon environment; and clients or technicians with documented sensitivity or allergy to thioglycolate can work with non-thio alternatives more safely.
explanations.d: Non-thio waves still use a disulfide bond-reducing mechanism; they would still face chemical compatibility concerns with hydroxide relaxer-processed hair for the same fundamental reasons as thio waves — the lanthionine bonds created by hydroxide relaxers interact unpredictably with reducing agents; this advantage is not supported.

questions.name: Hair Care Services
questions.objective: III.E.6c — Chemical waving/texturizing: Non-thio
questions.text: A client requests a permanent wave but reports a known allergy to thioglycolate-containing products. The barber's most appropriate response is to

answers.text: proceed with a standard alkaline thio wave at a lower concentration to minimize exposure
recommend a non-thio permanent wave formula that uses an alternative reducing agent the client is not sensitized to, after confirming the alternative does not share the same allergen
decline all future wave services permanently since all waves contain thioglycolate
apply the thio wave only to the ends of the hair, avoiding scalp contact

explanations.a: Using a lower concentration of a known allergen does not eliminate the allergic risk; in sensitized individuals, even trace amounts can trigger reactions; reducing concentration is not a safe strategy for managing documented thioglycolate allergy.
explanations.b: A thioglycolate allergy is a specific sensitivity to ammonium thioglycolate and related compounds; non-thio wave formulas using different reducing agents (cysteamine, ammonium bisulfite) do not contain thioglycolate and would not trigger the same allergic response in a thioglycolate-sensitized client; the barber should research the non-thio alternative's ingredient list to confirm it does not share cross-reactive compounds with the allergen, and may recommend a patch test with the non-thio formula before the full service.
explanations.c: Non-thio permanent waves do not contain thioglycolate; permanent waving is not absolutely contraindicated for all future services — only thioglycolate-containing formulas are contraindicated; alternative formulas may be safely offered.
explanations.d: Scalp-free application does not eliminate the risk from a thioglycolate allergy; the reducing agent can still contact the scalp through dripping or migration, and the allergen is still present in proximity to sensitive skin.

questions.name: Hair Care Services
questions.objective: III.E.6c — Chemical waving/texturizing: Non-thio
questions.text: The mechanism by which all permanent wave reducing agents (thio and non-thio) achieve curl formation is

answers.text: physical heat deforming the hair into the curl shape around the rod
depositing a polymer film on the cuticle surface that holds the curl shape
bleaching the melanin from the cortex, which reduces the curl-producing tension in the follicle
breaking the hair's disulfide bonds through reduction, physically reforming the hair around the rod, and then re-forming the disulfide bonds through oxidative neutralization in the new waved position

explanations.a: Physical heat deformation describes thermal styling (pressing combs, curling irons) — a temporary set that reverts when re-wetted; permanent waves work through irreversible chemical modification of covalent disulfide bonds, not through heat.
explanations.b: Polymer film deposition on the cuticle is how some styling products work (silicone coatings, film-forming polymers); permanent waves achieve their result through cortical chemistry, not surface coating.
explanations.c: Melanin bleaching (removal of pigment) has no effect on the hair's curl pattern; the curl is determined by the geometry of the disulfide bonds in the cortex and the shape of the follicle — not by melanin content.
explanations.d: All permanent wave systems — whether thio (ammonium thioglycolate, glyceryl monothioglycolate) or non-thio (cysteamine, bisulfite) — operate through the same fundamental three-step mechanism: (1) the reducing agent breaks the disulfide bonds in the cortex by adding hydrogen atoms (reduction), releasing the structural constraint of the cross-linked protein chains; (2) the softened hair is physically wrapped around the perm rod, adopting the rod's curved shape; (3) the oxidizing neutralizer removes the extra hydrogen atoms (oxidation), allowing the freed sulfur atoms on adjacent polypeptide chains to re-form disulfide bonds — this time in the new position imposed by the rod shape; the result is a permanent chemical change in the cortex architecture that maintains the curl until new growth appears.
